title: Make the review easier to follow.
intro: The brief was to make Change Stack easier to use without losing what it can do. I focused on reading the explanation, following the code and keeping track of the review. I reviewed the design with three developers through a mix of hands-on tasks and open feedback. Their feedback helped me revise the review flow. I haven’t completed a controlled comparison or measured improvements.
sections: In the original, summary points shared a broad code range and expanding the summary also moved the diff. I separated those actions: expand to read, then follow a statement link. The rest of the code stays visible. I’d check whether the highlight draws attention away from another branch. Summary complexity filters help reviewers choose what to read; they do not show finding severity or affected features.

Developers challenged the interrupted file flow and missing signals in my first version. I restored layer totals and recorded severity, and joined the files into one stream across seven layers. The original already scrolls continuously within a layer. Modified files retain equal Before/After panes; added files use full width. Inspect/Return restores the caller. The cost is keeping people oriented as they scroll.

Feedback exposed too many competing counts. Viewed is now the main progress measure, with Undo. It records a file check, not approval; submission remains a separate PR action. Summary Seen stays separate. Findings show severity beside resolution, and message counts include replies. Range notes retain their file, side and lines.

I kept the familiar Split / Unified comparison and now remember that choice and wrapping in this browser. Files lists the 52 changed files, not the whole repository. Tools explains unchanged context, wrapping and copy path. Overview offers a suggested route through this PR’s permission checks. Light, Dark and System remain optional preferences.
limits: All 52 pinned diffs and layer assignments are verified. Only selected source summaries and comments are included. The captured access finding has two replies whose text was not saved. Statement links are manually mapped. Security blast radius, Architecture impact, Verify and other secondary workflows link back to the source review; they are not implemented here.
next: Next I’d compare the same permission-review task in both versions, varying which comes first and recording missed checks, lost position and help needed. I’d also test collapsing viewed files without losing position and investigate how the security and verification views connect claims back to evidence.
